newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Time decay depresses debt volatility.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Time decay depresses debt volatility.

text.p: Implied volatility of bond options fell on Friday as the impact of the U.S. Independence Day holiday kicked in, brokers said.
"We had a half day closing in the U.S. yesterday and a lot of the U.S. clients did not come in," said Luke White, broker at FIMAT Futures in London.
"They altered their positions by telephone, and many did not alter their positions at all, as the result of the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting was expected."
The FOMC left U.S. interest rates unchanged after the second day of its July meeting on Wednesday.
The normal pattern of lower volatility on Fridays due to a two-day time decay going into the weekend was extended to four or five days this week, brokers said.
Implied volatility of at-the-money August Bund options was quoted at 4.40 percent against the LIFFE close of 4.50 percent on Thursday and 4.85 percent on Monday.
September Bund options were quoted at 4.93 percent compared with 4.85 percent on Thursday and 5.12 percent on Monday.
September Bund futures were at 102.45 at 1042 GMT, up 0.03.

Volatility in the out-of-the-money 101.50 strike picked up in heavy volume. Two firms were outright buyers of puts and there was also a large buyer of volatility, brokers said. The trade went through at a volatility level of 5.32 percent, they added.
"That was quite high, and caught the market unawares," said one broker from a U.S. bank in London.
Over 5,000 contracts traded in the 101.50 puts by 1042 GMT.
Implied volatility of BTP options was unchanged from Thursday's LIFFE close of 7.22 percent in thin volume, despite an active futures market, brokers said.
BTP futures hit an all-time high of 135.84 earlier in the session. September BTPs were trading at 135.67, up 0.13 on the day.
Meanwhile, volatility in options on the bonos future listed on MEFF was attracting attention, White said.
"Players have been going long volatility, which is down to 5.6 percent," he said.
